sentence_text: Part of what had happened is we’d forgotten why we had gone.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: We went because there were people who were responsible for 3,000 American deaths.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And so we decimated Al Qaida’s core leadership in the border regions between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: We then started to build up Afghan forces.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And we’re now in a position where we can transition out, because there’s no reason why Americans should die when Afghans are perfectly capable of defending their own country.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Now, that transition has to take place in a responsible fashion.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: We’ve been there a long time, and we’ve got to make sure that we and our coalition partners are pulling out responsibly and giving Afghans the capabilities that they need.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: But what I think the American people recognize is after a decade of war it’s time to do some nation building here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And what we can now do is free up some resources, to, for example, put Americans back to work, especially our veterans, rebuilding our roads, our bridges, our schools, making sure that, you know, our veterans are getting the care that they need when it comes to post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injury, making sure that the certifications that they need for good jobs of the future are in place.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: You know, I was having lunch with some — a veteran in Minnesota who had been a medic dealing with the most extreme circumstances.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: When he came home and he wanted to become a nurse, he had to start from scratch.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And what we’ve said is let’s change those certifications.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: The first lady has done great work with an organization called Joining Forces putting our veterans back to work.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And as a consequence, veterans’ unemployment is actually now lower than general population.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: It was higher when I came into office.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: So those are the kinds of things that we can now do because we’re making that transition in Afghanistan.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: All right.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: Let me go to Governor Romney because you talked about Pakistan and what needs to be done there.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: General Allen, our commander in Afghanistan, says that Americans continue to die at the hands of groups who are supported by Pakistan.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: We know that Pakistan has arrested the doctor who helped us catch Obama bin Laden.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: It still provides safe haven for terrorists, yet we continue to give Pakistan billions of dollars.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: Is it time for us to divorce Pakistan?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: No, it’s not time to divorce a nation on Earth that has 100 nuclear weapons and is on the way to double that at some point, a nation that has serious threats from terrorist groups within its nation, as I indicated before, the Taliban, Haqqani Network.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It’s a nation that’s not like — like others and it does not have a civilian leadership that is calling the shots there.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: You have the ISI, their intelligence organization, is probably the most powerful of the — of three branches there.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Then you have the military and then you have the civilian government.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: This is a nation, which, if it falls apart, if it — if it becomes a failed state, there are nuclear weapons there and you’ve got — you’ve got terrorists there who could grab their — their hands onto those nuclear weapons.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: This is — this is an important part of the world for us.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Pakistan is — is technically an ally, and they’re not acting very much like an ally right now.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: But we have some work to do.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And I — I don’t blame the administration for the fact that the relationship with Pakistan is strained.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We — we had to go into Pakistan.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We had to go in there to get Osama bin Laden.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: That was the right thing to do.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And — and that upset them, but obviously there was a great deal of anger even before that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: But we’re going to have to work with the — with the people in Pakistan to try and help them move to a more responsible course than the one that they’re on.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And it’s important for them.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It’s important for the nuclear weapons.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It’s important for the success of Afghanistan.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Because inside Pakistan, you have a — a large group of Pashtun that are — that are Taliban.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They’re going to come rushing back in to Afghanistan when we go.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And that’s one of the reasons the Afghan Security Forces have so much work to do to be able to fight against that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: But it’s important for us to recognize that we can’t just walk away from Pakistan.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: But we do need to make sure that as we — as we send support for them, that this is tied to them making progress on — on matters that would lead them to becoming a civil society.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: Let — let me ask you, Governor because we know President Obama’s position on this, what is — what is your position on the use of drones?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Well I believe we should use any and all means necessary to take out people who pose a threat to us and our friends around the world.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And it’s widely reported that drones are being used in drone strikes, and I support that and entirely, and feel the president was right to up the usage of that technology, and believe that we should continue to use it, to continue to go after the people that represent a threat to this nation and to our friends.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: But let me also note that as I said earlier, we’re going to have to do more than just going after leaders and — and killing bad guys, important as that is.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We’re also going to have to have a farm more effective and comprehensive strategy to help move the world away from terror and Islamic extremism.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We haven’t done that yet.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We talk a lot about these things, but you look at the — the record, you look at the record.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: You look at the record of the last four years and say is Iran closer to a bomb?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Yes.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Is the Middle East in tumult?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Yes.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Is — is al-Qaida on the run, on its heels?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: No.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Is — are Israel and the Palestinians closer to reaching a peace agreement?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: No, they haven’t had talks in two years.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We have not seen the progress we need to have, and I’m convinced that with strong leadership and an effort to build a strategy based upon helping these nations reject extremism, we can see the kind of peace and prosperity the world demands.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Well, keep in mind our strategy wasn’t just going after bin Laden.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: We created partnerships throughout the region to deal with extremism in Somalia, in Yemen, in Pakistan.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And what we’ve also done is engaged these governments in the kind of reforms that are actually going to make a difference in people’s lives day to day, to make sure that their governments aren’t corrupt, to make sure that they’re treating women with the kind of respect and dignity that every nation that succeeds has shown and to make sure that they’ve got a free market system that works.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: So across the board, we are engaging them in building capacity in these countries.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And we have stood on the side of democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: One thing I think Americans should be proud of, when Tunisians began to protest, this nation — me, my administration — stood with them earlier than just about any country.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: In Egypt we stood on the side of democracy.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: In Libya we stood on the side of the people.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And as a consequence, there’s no doubt that attitudes about Americans have changed.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: But there are always going to be elements in these countries that potentially threaten the United States.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And we want to shrink those groups and those networks and we can do that.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: But we’re always also going to have to maintain vigilance when it comes to terrorist activities.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: The truth, though, is that Al Qaeda is much weaker than it was when I came into office.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And they don’t have the same capacities to attack the U.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: homeland and our allies as they did four years ago.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: Let’s — let’s go to the next segment, because it’s a very important one.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: It is the rise of China and future challenges for America.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: I want to just begin this by asking both of you, and Mr.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: President, you — you go first this time.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: What do you believe is the greatest future threat to the national security of this country?

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Well, I think it will continue to be terrorist networks.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: We have to remain vigilant, as I just said.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: But with respect to China, China is both an adversary, but also a potential partner in the international community if it’s following the rules.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: So my attitude coming into office was that we are going to insist that China plays by the same rules as everybody else.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: I know Americans had seen jobs being shipped overseas; businesses and workers not getting a level playing field when it came to trade.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And that’s the reason why I set up a trade task force to go after cheaters when it came to international trade.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: That’s the reason why we have brought more cases against China for violating trade rules than the other — the previous administration had done in two terms.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And we’ve won just about every case that we’ve filed, that has been decided.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: In fact, just recently steelworkers in Ohio and throughout the Midwest — Pennsylvania — are in a position now to sell steel to China because we won that case.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: We had a tire case in which they were flooding us with cheap domestic tires — or — or cheap Chinese tires.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And we put a stop to it and as a consequence saved jobs throughout America.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: I have to say that Governor Romney criticized me for being too tough in that tire case; said this wouldn’t be good for American workers and that it would be protectionist.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: But I tell you, those workers don’t feel that way.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: They feel as if they had finally an administration who was going to take this issue seriously.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Over the long term, in order for us to compete with China, we’ve also got to make sure, though, that we’re taking — taking care of business here at home.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: If we don’t have the best education system in the world, if we don’t continue to put money into research and technology that will allow us to create great businesses here in the United States, that’s how we lose the competition.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And, unfortunately, Governor Romney’s budget and his proposals would not allow us to make those investments.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: All right.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: Governor?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Well, first of all, it’s not government that makes business successful.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It’s not government investments that makes businesses grow and hire people.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Let me also note that the greatest threat that the world faces, the greatest national security threat is a nuclear Iran.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Let’s talk about China.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: China has an interest that’s very much like ours in one respect, and that is they want a stable world.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They don’t want war.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They don’t want to see protectionism.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They don’t want to see the world break out into — into various forms of chaos, because they have to — they have to manufacture goods and put people to work and they have about 20,000 — 20 million, rather, people coming out of the farms every year coming into the cities, needing jobs.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: So they want the economy to work and the world to be free and open.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And so we can be a partner with China.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We don’t have to be an adversary in any way, shape or form.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We can work with them, we can collaborate with them, if they’re willing to be responsible.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Now, they look at us and say, Is it a good idea to be with America?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: How strong are we going to be?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: How strong is our economy?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They look at the fact that we owe ’em a trillion dollars and owe other people $16 trillion in total, including that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They look at our — our decision to — to cut back on our military capabilities.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: A trillion dollars.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: The secretary of defense called these trillion dollars of cuts to our military devastating.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It’s not my term, it’s the president’s own secretary of defense called these trillion dollars of cuts to our military devastating.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It’s not my term, it’s the president’s own Secretary of Defense, called them devastating.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They look at America’s commitments around the world and they see what’s happening, and they say, well, OK.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Is America going to be strong?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And the answer is, yes, if I’m president, America will be very strong.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We’ll also make sure that we have trade relations with China that work for us.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I’ve watched year in and year out as companies have shut down and people have lost their jobs because China has not played by the same rules, in part by holding down artificially the value of their currency.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It holds down the prices of their goods.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It means our goods aren’t as competitive and we lose jobs.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: That’s got to end.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They’re making some progress; they need to make more.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: That’s why on day one, i will label them a currency manipulator, which allows us to apply tariffs where they’re taking jobs.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They’re stealing our intellectual property, our patents, our designs, our technology, hacking into our computers, counterfeiting our goods.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They have to understand we want to trade with them.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We want a world that’s stable.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We like free enterprise, but you got to play by the rules.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: Well, Governor, let me just ask you.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: If you declare them a currency manipulator on day one, some people are — say you’re just going to start a trade war with China on day one.

speaker: Schieffer
sentence_text: Is that — isn’t there a risk that that could happen?

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Well, they sell us about this much stuff every year, and we sell them about this much stuff every year.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: So it’s pretty clear who doesn’t want a trade war.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And there’s one going on right now, which we don’t know about it.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It’s a silent one.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And they’re winning.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We have enormous trade imbalance with China, and it’s worse this year than last year, and it’s worse last year than the year before.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And so we have to understand that we can’t just surrender and lose jobs year in and year out.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We have to say to our friend in China, look, you guys are playing aggressively.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: We understand it.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: But this can’t keep on going.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: You can’t keep on holding down the value of your currency, stealing our intellectual property, counterfeiting our products, selling them around the world, even to the United States.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I was with one company that makes valves and — and process industries and they said, look, we were — we were having some valves coming in that — that were broken and we had to repair them under warranty and we looked them and — and they had our serial number on them.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And then we noticed that there was more than one with that same serial number.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: They were counterfeit products being made overseas with the same serial number as a U.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: company, the same packaging, these were being sold into our market and around the world as if they were made by the U.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: competitor.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: This can’t go on.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I want a great relationship with China.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: China can be our partner, but — but that doesn’t mean they can just roll all over us and steal our jobs on an unfair basis.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Well, Governor Romney’s right, you are familiar with jobs being shipped overseas because you invested in companies that were shipping jobs overseas.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And, you know, that’s — you’re right.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: I mean that’s how our free market works.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: But I’ve made a different bet on American workers.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: If we had taken your advice Governor Romney about our auto industry, we’d be buying cars from China instead of selling cars to China.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: If we take your advice with respect to how we change our tax codes so that companies that earn profits overseas don’t pay U.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: taxes compared to companies here that are paying taxes.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Now that’s estimated to create 800,000 jobs, the problem is they won’t be here, they’ll be in places like China.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And if we’re not making investments in education and basic research, which is not something that the private sector is doing at a sufficient pace right now and has never done, then we will lose the in things like clean energy technology.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Now with respect to what we’ve done with China already, U.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: exports have doubled since I came into office, to China and actually currencies are at their most advantageous point for U.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: exporters since 1993.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: We absolutely have to make more progress and that’s why we’re going to keep on pressing.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And when it comes to our military and Chinese security, part of the reason that we were able to pivot to the Asia-Pacific region after having ended the war in Iraq and transitioning out of Afghanistan, is precisely because this is going to be a massive growth area in the future.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And we believe China can be a partner, but we’re also sending a very clear signal that America is a Pacific power; that we are going to have a presence there.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: We are working with countries in the region to make sure, for example, that ships can pass through; that commerce continues.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: And we’re organizing trade relations with countries other than China so that China starts feeling more pressure about meeting basic international standards.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: That’s the kind of leadership we’ve shown in the region.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: That’s the kind of leadership that we’ll continue to show.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I just want to take one of those points, again, attacking me as not talking about an agenda for — for getting more trade and opening up more jobs in this country.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: But the president mentioned the auto industry and that somehow I would be in favor of jobs being elsewhere.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Nothing could be further from the truth.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I’m a son of Detroit.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I was born in Detroit.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: My dad was head of a car company.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I like American cars.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And I would do nothing to hurt the U.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: auto industry.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: My plan to get the industry on its feet when it was in real trouble was not to start writing checks.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: It was President Bush that wrote the first checks.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I disagree with that.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I said they need — these companies need to go through a managed bankruptcy.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And in that process, they can get government help and government guarantees, but they need to go through bankruptcy to get rid of excess cost and the debt burden that they’d — they’d built up.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And fortunately…

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Governor Romney, that’s not what you said…

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Governor Romney, you did not…

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: You can take a look at the op-ed…

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: You did not say that you would provide government help.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I said that we would provide guarantees, and — and that was what was able to allow these companies to go through bankruptcy, to come out of bankruptcy.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Under no circumstances would I do anything other than to help this industry get on its feet.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: And the idea that has been suggested that I would liquidate the industry, of course not.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: Of course not.

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Let’s check the record.

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: That’s the height of silliness…

speaker: Barack Obama
sentence_text: Let — let — let’s…

speaker: Mitt Romney
sentence_text: I have never said I would liquidate…

speaker: Obam
